width.meaning: the validator's share of stake this epoch, compressed into a band

height.meaning: square root of the validator's share of stake this epoch

colour.meaning: kind of account: staking pool, liquid-staking contract, or unknown

outline.meaning: solid when the name is self-declared (pool-details.near or a named account id) or verified, dashed when inferred, none when unknown

segments.meaning: who stands behind each pool: its delegations split into other delegators, accounts with 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts and lockups (delegations under 1,000 NEAR are folded per pool and class, as coverage declares)

order.meaning: largest stake first, clockwise from the top

interpretation.summary: Stake decides who produces NEAR's blocks. 9 of the 371 seated validators together hold more than a third of it, enough to stall the chain. Behind each pool stand its backers: many small delegators, a few large accounts, liquid-staking contracts and lockups.

power_means.claim: A validator's power is its stake in the current epoch: it sets how many blocks and chunks the validator produces.
9 validators together pass the one-third threshold that BFT consensus needs to halt.
Stake is lent to a pool by its delegators; they can move it, so they share the pool's power.

mappings.why: Share of stake is the power that counts here, compressed into a band so small validators stay visible.
Bar height repeats the share, on a square-root scale, so the largest validators stand out.
Kind of account tells pools from liquid-staking entities.
Pool names are self-declared on-chain, so they are drawn as self-declared, never verified.
Each bar is cut into the backers of the pool: other delegators, accounts with 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts and lockups.
Largest first, clockwise from the top, so the validators that matter most are read first.

conflicts: House of Stake voting power (veNEAR) is a second kind of power on NEAR; this flower draws block-production stake only.
unknowns: Who controls the large implicit (hex) delegators: most of the biggest delegators have no public name.
Who owns the lockup contracts: their owners were not resolved.
Whether several pools are run by one operator: pools are not merged without evidence.
inferred: A named .near account is a self-declared name, not a verified identity.
